text: The 2010 UEFA Champions League final was an association football match played at the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, home of Real Madrid, on 22 May 2010, to determine the winners of the 2009–10 UEFA Champions League. It was the first Champions League final to be held on a weekend, rather than the traditional Wednesday. The match was won by Inter Milan, who defeated Bayern Munich 2–0, completing the treble—a feat never before achieved by any team from either Italy or Germany. This victory marked Inter's third European Cup title and their first since 1965; it was also their first final appearance since 1972 and the first time an Italian team had reached the final since A.C. Milan's win in 2007. Bayern, who had last won the competition in 2001, were the first German side to reach the final since Bayer Leverkusen in 2002. The 2010 final was the first not to feature an English side since Porto beat Monaco in 2004, due to Manchester United being eliminated by Bayern Munich in the quarter-finals on away goals. The Santiago Bernabéu Stadium had previously hosted three European Cup finals: in 1957, 1969, and 1980. The venue was selected by the UEFA Executive Committee in Vaduz, Liechtenstein, on 28 March 2008, based on criteria including stadium capacity, facilities, and security, and the decision to play the final on a Saturday was made at a meeting in Lucerne on 30 November 2007. The stadium, opened in 1947, had a capacity exceeding 75,000 initially, increased to 125,000 in 1954, reduced to 90,800 after renovations for the 1982 FIFA World Cup, and later reduced to just over 75,000 after conversion to an all-seater stadium in 1998, with a slight increase to just over 80,000 in 2006; only around 75,000 seats were available for the 2010 final. Each finalist was allocated 21,000 tickets, with 11,000 available to the general public, and applications ran from 8 to 19 March 2010 via a random lottery, including 2,000 children's tickets from each club and 1,000 from the public, plus 500 for children at the UEFA Champions Festival. A ticketing launch event was held in Madrid on 5 March 2010, attended by Emilio Butragueño, Esperanza Aguirre, and representatives from UEFA, the Royal Spanish Football Federation, and Real Madrid, with Aguirre receiving the first ticket from players Cristiano Ronaldo and Raúl. A trophy handover ceremony took place at the Palacio de Cibeles on 16 April 2010, where Johan Cruyff and Joan Laporta returned the trophy to UEFA president Michel Platini, who then handed it to Ángel María Villar Llona and Alberto Ruiz-Gallardón for display until the final. The official match ball, the Adidas Finale Madrid, was unveiled on 9 March 2010 and featured a "Starball" design with gold stars incorporating elements from the logos of the last 10 Champions League finals, each with a red border referencing the Spanish flag and a white base matching Real Madrid's kit. The referee was Howard Webb of England, supported by Darren Cann and Mike Mullarkey as assistant referees and Martin Atkinson as the fourth official, all from England. Inter started without any Italian players, while Bayern began with five German internationals, including Franck Ribéry, who was suspended for three matches after being sent off in the semi-final, and Thiago Motta, suspended for two matches. The match opened with the UEFA Champions Festival on 15 May 2010 at Parque del Retiro, culminating in a match between former Spanish players and European ex-professionals on the final day. The UEFA Champions League Anthem was performed by Peruvian tenor Juan Diego Flórez. Inter won 2–0 with both goals scored by Diego Milito in the 35th and 70th minutes; the first followed a long clearance flicked down by Milito to Wesley Sneijder, who returned the pass to Milito, and the second came after Milito collected a pass from Samuel Eto'o and beat Daniel Van Buyten. Milito was substituted before the end of the match and was applauded by Inter supporters, stating the win brought "incredible happiness" and that his team deserved the victory. Bayern captain Mark van Bommel acknowledged Inter as the "most effective team" due to their counter-attacking strategy. José Mourinho, who had previously managed Porto in 2004 and won the Champions League with Ajax in 1995, became only the third manager in European Cup history to win with two clubs, following Ernst Happel and Ottmar Hitzfeld. As winners, Inter played against Atlético Madrid, the 2009–10 UEFA Europa League winners, in the 2010 UEFA Super Cup, losing 2–0 with goals from José Antonio Reyes and Sergio Agüero, and also entered the 2010 FIFA Club World Cup, where they beat Seongnam Ilhwa Chunma 3–0 in the semi-finals and then defeated TP Mazembe 3–0 in the final to win the title. Inter secured the treble for the first time in Italian football history after winning the Coppa Italia and Serie A titles in 2010. As a result of the victory, Italy retained its fourth berth in the 2010–11 UEFA Champions League, while if Bayern had won or the match had gone to penalties, Germany would have overtaken Italy and gained an extra entry. José Mourinho resigned as Inter manager on 28 May to join Real Madrid for the 2010–11 season, citing a desire to become the first manager to win the Champions League with three clubs, though he was unable to achieve this, being eliminated in three successive semi-finals before returning to Chelsea in June 2013, with Carlo Ancelotti replacing him at Real Madrid, who won their tenth title in his first season. UEFA Man of the Match was Diego Milito (Inter Milan), and Fans' Man of the Match was Wesley Sneijder (Inter Milan).
